summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly in index.html on the first turn (~26s), without invoking any skill. No brainstorming skill invocation appears in the session log.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied per the session log and the resulting file. The only anomaly is the missing token-usage artifact, which I report as an observation rather than a criterion failure.

observations.description: No coding-agent-token-usage.json was produced anywhere under the run results directory (find ... -name '*token-usage*' returned nothing, both before and after /exit). The story's headline cost metric therefore has no artifact to read.
Agent added two sample <li> task items ('Write the tasks page', 'Add a checkbox') plus CSS styling, slightly more than the 'nothing fancy' request, but still mechanical and no JS.
Launch required stepping through four first-run prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) with 'No, exit' preselected as the default on both confirm dialogs.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ Done — index.html:1 now has a task list where each item is a <label class="task"> wrapping a native <input type="checkbox">' and '✻ Brewed for 26s'. Tool calls in session log were only Read/Edit/Bash (grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' → 1 Bash, 1 Edit, 1 Read). index.html line 31/37: '<input type="checkbox">'. No clarifying questions were asked.

grep -o '"name":"Skill"' on the session jsonl returned 0. The only 'brainstorm' matches in the log are in the injected system prompt text and the initial skill_listing attachment ('- hyperpowers:brainstorming'), not a tool invocation.
